## Purpose and entry points
DeepWiki-Open generates interactive documentation, diagrams, and code maps for GitHub, GitLab, or BitBucket repositories. It is a Next.js frontend backed by a Python API. Browser entry points are the landing page and repository-scoped views in `src/app/page.tsx`, `src/app/[owner]/[repo]/page.tsx`, plus workshop and slides routes. Python service startup is `api/main.py`; container deployment is defined by `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml`.

## Frontend application and API proxy boundary
The Next.js app collects repository and model settings, renders generated wiki content, code views, and chat, and exposes same-origin route handlers that forward work to the backend. Key UI/API boundary paths are `src/components/Ask.tsx`, `src/components/WikiTreeView.tsx`, `src/app/api/repo/prepare/route.ts`, and `src/app/api/wiki/tasks/route.ts`. This isolates browser clients from backend service URLs and supports streaming task/chat endpoints.

## Backend HTTP orchestration
The Python API organizes public operations into routers for repository preparation, chat, code maps, wiki generation, system/model configuration, and authentication. `api/main.py` composes the service; `api/routers/repo.py`, `api/routers/chat.py`, `api/routers/codemap.py`, and `api/routers/wiki.py` define the primary API surface. Typed request/response contracts are centralized in `api/schemas/`, particularly `api/schemas/repo.py`, `api/schemas/chat.py`, and `api/schemas/wiki.py`.

## Repository ingestion and analysis
Repository handling is a distinct boundary that accepts remote repository identity and prepares material for downstream generation. `api/repository.py` owns repository access/normalization, while `api/services/codemap.py` produces code-centric guided-tour output. The frontend initiates this lifecycle through `src/utils/prepareRepo.ts` and presents code exploration through `src/components/CodeMap.tsx` and `src/components/CodeViewer.tsx`.

## Wiki generation pipeline
Wiki work is asynchronous and task-oriented: structural planning, content generation, persistence/I/O, and task status/streaming are separated. The main modules are `api/services/wiki/structure.py`, `api/services/wiki/content.py`, `api/services/wiki/tasks.py`, and `api/services/wiki/io.py`. Browser consumers list projects and poll or stream individual task progress via `src/app/api/wiki/projects/route.ts` and `src/app/api/wiki/tasks/[task_id]/stream/route.ts`.

## RAG and conversational research
Chat combines repository-grounded retrieval with model generation. `api/rag/pipeline.py` and `api/rag/rag.py` form the retrieval-augmented-generation layer; `api/chat/_stream.py` provides streamed output and `api/chat/_prompts.py` contains chat-specific prompt assembly. `api/services/research.py` is the higher-level research service, surfaced in the UI by `src/components/Ask.tsx`.

## Models, providers, and runtime infrastructure
Model access is provider-adapted rather than hardwired: `api/clients/litellm.py`, `api/clients/ollama.py`, `api/clients/anthropic.py`, `api/clients/bedrock.py`, `api/clients/dashscope.py`, and `api/clients/google_embedder.py` cover generation and embedding backends. Runtime selection/configuration is managed by `api/config.py` and JSON definitions such as `api/config/generator.json` and `api/config/embedder.json`. Docker supports the default stack plus LiteLLM and local Ollama variants through `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose-litellm.yml`, `Dockerfile-litellm`, and `Dockerfile-ollama-local`.
